title: Unescaped feed and article metadata is written into EPUB XHTML

evidence.quote:
return RawArticle(
                title: title,
                link: link,
                author: item.author ?? item.dublinCore?.dcCreator ?? "",

public let title: String
    public let author: String
    public let content: String
    public let originalUrl: String
    public let feedName: String

let authorHTML = article.author.isEmpty ? "" : "

By \(article.author)

\n " \(article.title)

Read original

reasoning: RSS/Atom/JSON feed metadata is external input, but the EPUB builder interpolates title, author, feedName, and originalUrl directly into XHTML text and attributes. Characters such as &, <, >, and quotes can produce malformed EPUB chapters; quote characters in originalUrl can also break out of the href attribute and inject additional markup/attributes. The file already has escapeXML for TOC text, but these chapter paths do not use it.
reproduction: Create a ProcessedArticle with title `A & B `, author `x
recommendation: Escape metadata before inserting it into XHTML text nodes and attributes. Keep article.content as a separate trusted/sanitized HTML path, but escape title, author, feedName, and href values consistently, and validate or safely encode originalUrl before writing it into an attribute.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Modules/Domain/Tests/DomainTests/FeedTests.swift only checks simple ASCII model initialization and ProcessedArticle conversion; it does not generate EPUB output or use metadata containing XML/HTML special characters.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an EPUBBuilder test that generates a chapter from article/feed metadata containing `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'`, then parses the generated XHTML as XML and asserts the metadata is escaped and no extra attributes/elements are introduced.
minimumFixScope: EPUBBuilder chapter/section rendering plus focused EPUB generation tests for escaped metadata.
